**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Section 15 "Assignment or Transfer" (p0080).**

What I found:

- **Section 15 is the only assignment provision.** It bars either party from assigning without the other's prior written approval, with a single carve-out for "an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate."
- **No change-of-control language exists anywhere in the Agreement** (searched "change of control", "assign", and reviewed the termination provisions at §§ 13–14). TrueLink therefore has no termination or re-pricing right triggered by our change of control — that limb of the rule is satisfied.

Why it fails the fallback on material terms:

1. **No successor / M&A carve-out for Client.** The affiliate carve-out does not cover a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, so a corporate transaction would need TrueLink's sign-off. The rule treats a prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out as walk-away territory.
2. **Absolute consent discretion.** There is no "not unreasonably withheld" standard, which even the fallback requires.

Redline applied (validated `ok:true`, modelled on the approved *Keystone ERP* precedent) — a single-sentence edit that preserves the mutual structure and the existing affiliate carve-out:

> …without the prior written approval of the other party, **which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed**, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate **or, in the case of Client, to a successor in a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of substantially all of its assets**.

One point noted but deliberately not flagged: the preferred position also bars the Vendor from assigning to a Client competitor. Given the clause is otherwise mutual and already requires our consent to any TrueLink assignment, pressing that sub-element would be disproportionate — it is recorded in the rationale rather than redlined.
